summary:
AstraHealth is a health-monitoring prototype for astronauts on long-duration missions, where radiation, altered gravity, isolation, and distance from Earth can make it harder to notice changes and get timely support. It brings simulated physiological, wellbeing, and cabin-environment readings into a live dashboard with trends, alerts, scenario views, and an overall risk summary. Astronauts can record daily mood and sleep check-ins, complete structured wellbeing assessments, and receive informational recommendations based on available assessment, check-in, and metric context. An optional locally hosted conversational assistant supports further interaction.

The onboard mission-control interface lets crew queue text updates or requests for professional or additional help. A separate Earth-side dashboard simulates contact windows, message delivery, and a shared view of registered crew metrics. This gives the project a way to demonstrate both self-monitoring in space and communication with Earth when contact is available.

AstraHealth matters because it explores how clear, timely health information could support crew autonomy when Earth is far away.
details:
AstraHealth is a spaceflight health-monitoring prototype that brings astronaut health, wellbeing, and cabin-environment information into one dashboard. It displays simulated readings and trends, highlights rule-based alerts, and supports scenario changes such as elevated CO₂ or prolonged isolation. Astronauts can also record daily mood and sleep check-ins, complete structured wellbeing assessments, and receive informational recommendations based on the available data. An optional local conversational assistant supports follow-up. Through a separate mission-control interface, crew can queue text updates or requests for help; an Earth-side dashboard simulates contact windows, message delivery, and a summary of registered crew metrics.

The project aims to help crews notice changes, understand their readings, and prepare clear updates for Earth when communication is available. Its creative approach combines physical and environmental monitoring with wellbeing tools and simulated communication in a single mission workflow.

We built the web interface with React and TypeScript, backend services with Python and FastAPI, and containerized the services with Docker Compose. SQLite stores service data. Simulated inputs let us demonstrate changing conditions without physical sensors or real mission data; an optional Ollama service supports local conversational AI. Several models coexist within the platform and provide insights into metrics and their meanings.

We considered readability, sensor availability, privacy, communication delays, and the limits of automated guidance.
projectRefs: Why do we conduct science experiments in space?
